D1.title: IMU on QWIIC
D1.heading: Find a BMI270 on the QWIIC bus
D1.goal: Plug a BMI270 motion sensor into the QWIIC connector, scan the bus and read its chip ID register to prove it is the part you think it is.
steps: Unplug USB and connect the BMI270 with a QWIIC cable, or with jumpers to the header pins in the table.
Run the command. The scan prints found 0x68 (or 0x69).
D1.note: The Pulsar C5 has no pull-ups on QWIIC. Most sensor boards carry their own; with a bare chip, add 4.7 kΩ from SDA and SCL to 3V3. On the C6 this lab used GPIO6/7.

D2.title: OLED light graph
D2.heading: Two devices on one bus: OLED and light sensor
D2.goal: Put an SSD1306 OLED (0x3C) and a TEMT6000 light sensor (0x20) on the same QWIIC bus, and plot the last six seconds of light on the screen.
steps: Install Adafruit SSD1306, Adafruit GFX Library and DevLabDDP from the Library Manager.
Unplug USB and wire both boards in parallel, or chain them with QWIIC cables.
Run the command. The monitor confirms a TEMT6000 with ID 0x0102 at 0x20.
Cover the sensor, then shine a light on it: the graph drops and climbs.
D2.note: The reading is a relative 12-bit level, not lux: calibrate against a light meter before quoting units.

micropython.label: MicroPython
micropython.goal: Read the TEMT6000 DDP over QWIIC and plot its recent light readings on an SSD1306 OLED with MicroPython.
steps: Unplug USB and connect the OLED and TEMT6000 DDP to the QWIIC bus. Use 3V3 and GND as shown.
Open Code, connect the serial REPL and select Install ssd1306.py. This saves the display driver on the board.
Run oled_light.py. The terminal identifies the TEMT6000 as 0x0102, and the OLED draws its readings.
Cover the sensor, then shine a light on it. The graph should change; press Stop when finished.
micropython.note: This D2 graph needs a TEMT6000 DDP sensor. To turn on the OLED alone, use Display lesson O1. The sensor reports a relative 12-bit value, not lux. Install ssd1306.py once from the code workspace before running.

D3.title: Analog temperature
D3.heading: From millivolts to degrees with a TMP235
D3.goal: Read a TMP235 analog temperature sensor on A2, convert millivolts to °C and smooth the result with a simple filter.
steps: Unplug USB and wire the sensor as in the table.
Run the command and open the Serial Plotter.
Pinch the sensor: the raw line jumps, the filtered line follows smoothly.
D3.note: TMP235: Vout = 500 mV + 10 mV/°C, so 750 mV is 25 °C. analogReadMilliVolts() already applies the chip's factory ADC calibration.
